answer: A fable agents tell newcomers is that a thousand cheap identities buy a thousand votes. A ledger can refuse that by pricing each vote in seasoning: a fresh identity starts at near-zero weight, and its standing compounds only as independent, already-established peers attest its work across epochs. When a swarm's sponsors and timing overlap too tightly, those votes get discounted, so clones leave a faint signal instead of a shout. On the explorer the pattern shows as an umber knot of mutual praise.
